reviewText: This CD is an incredible mix of upbeat warfare worship and quiet meditative worship.  I can be on my face one moment and dancing in praise the next.  Misty has been featured on some other albums as part of a collection of worship leaders but this is her first solo album.  I hope she continues writing and publishing songs.  I'd buy future albums just on the basis of my experience with this one.

In December 2003, I went to the onething conference in Kansas City, MO. I heard plenty of sermons and lots of great worship, so much that it's all kind of a blur. One worship leader stood out to my sleep-deprived self, though -- Misty Edwards. I bought her CD soon after the conference and could not stop listening to it. Her unique voice and enunciation, passion for God, and worship style keep me reaching for this CD over other music.

Misty has such a heart for the Lord. She's a worship leader at the International House of Prayer in KC (if you're ever in the area, go to her Friday night worship set at 10:00) and sings her heart out on multiple sets per week. She gives everything she has every time she worships. Every. Time. This CD is no different in that respect.

She does have a different worship style than that of ETERNITY. The songs here are fairly straightforward, whereas in "real life" she tends to just worship in the Spirit after a few verses, singing random bits from the Bible and other songs. Also, her worship sets are not quite as rock-influenced as this CD. It is kind of nice to hear her songs all the way through for once, but be aware that this is not the complete Misty experience. :D

Anyway, I see that right now there are (sadly) no track samples, so I'll briefly describe each track.
1) Break the Chains: A song about breaking away from everything that holds her back from being satisfied with God.
2) Until the Day Breaks: Taken from Song of Solomon 4:6, Misty describes waiting for the Bridegroom -- the "face that I crave...[the] presence that I long for."
3) Oh How We Want You To Come!: The title's pretty self-explanatory. One of the more rock-inspired songs.
4) Eternity: The title track of the CD and one of Misty's favorite songs to quote, especially this part: "All flesh is grass, fading away. / Only You last, only You remain."
5) Simple Devotion: I cannot get enough of this song. She keeps seeking the Lord, wishing only to rest in Him, and He responds with gladness. "Angels, O angels, look and see! / Through that cloud of unknowing, / She's gazing at Me!" This is one of the best songs on the CD -- just Misty, her keyboard, and the God she's worshipping.
6) Just in Time: Describes the feelings of pursuing Jesus -- falling, tumbling -- and wondering what's going to happen. Misty takes one of the most beautiful passages from Ecclesiastes (3:11) and uses it as the chorus: "You make all things beautiful, just in time." Gorgeous song.
7)All That I Want: Again, self-explanatory. Mellow feel.
8) Vow: More from Ecclesiastes -- 3:1-8, this time. Devoted to God through all seasons.
9) Let Me Love You More: More pop-influenced than some of the others, this song pleads with the Father. "Oh, won't You / Let me love You more / This is all that I desire...."
10) I49: As the liner notes explain, this is a prophetic song about God's heart for Israel. He will not forget His people. Based on Isaiah 49.
11) Only a Shadow: One of the more rockin' songs. It's about remembering that our life here on earth is but a shadow of things to come. I always crank this song up when it comes on.
12) Glance: Falling in love with the Lamb. Wow.
As I said earlier, this CD does not demonstrate Misty's full worship style, but it's more than adequate until IHOP begins releasing recordings of worship sets (possibly this summer, according to an IHOP sound engineer I talked to in late June). I advise anyone who loves heartfelt worship to get ETERNITY. Turn it up, open your Bible, close your eyes, and just let Misty's lyrics and music minister to you. "This is my simple devotion...."
summary: Eternity's eternal song is drawing me / Is calling me away

reviewText: What can I say about Shotgun Angel? It is a classic in Christian rock. This album was my introduction to a great Christian rock band who blazed the way for a lot of the alternative Christian bands even today. Terry Scott Taylor is a lyrical genious and it shows on this album. If you're into the country rock of the 70s by bands like Flying Burrito Brothers, NRPS, The Eagles, CSN, then you should dig this album.

This is classic Country Rock Style album by one of the most talented and relative bands in the Christian Music Scene today.  We are treated to the classic Shotgun Angel album ...all songs are superb and well produced and then we get the bonus disc that has 26 tracks that were recorded back when the album was taking shape.  Even though these extra song tracks are from long ago, they sound so fresh and clear that it is hard to believe this was over 30 + years ago.  It also reflects highly on the band Daniel Amos.  I enjoyed listening to these recorded demos and alt. mixes, it gives added insight to how the songs had progressed to the finished product.  A well informative booklet with many newly seen photos also add to the whole project.  Overall a great gift to us, the fans and members of the faith.

My first encounter with Shotgun Angel was on a 2000 mile road trip with a couple of buddies, in a Chevy Monster truck.  Shotgun Angel was our theme song, on an adventure taking us from Texas to Chicago Gangland to home.  We really needed a Shotgun Angel on that trip (any trip combining a hopped up Chevy Big Block with Billy Brink or Michael O's driving needed an Angel).
Daniel Amos's 1st Album was a great country-country Rock Album, this album transitioned from country rock on the front side, to almost classical to Rock, especially with the end times rock opera theme on the flip-side.

This is in my opinion the best Daniel Amos Album, and would make my top ten list of best Christian Rock Albums of all time.  Buy it for more than it's place in music history, buy it because this album would be considered great in any era.

Will McDonald
summary: One of Best all time Christian Rock Albums

reviewText: I had been waiting for over 20 years for this digital (CD) collector's version re-issue. My cassette tape of this album died that long ago after my vinyl versions were gone years before the cassettes. DANIEL AMOS was one of the first ground breaking Christian "rock" bands. I cannot classify the music genre on this SHOTGUN ANGEL album as "rock" but is more country or country rock(think EAGLES,PURE PRAIRIE LEAGUE,POCO,etc) in style with a myriad of other sounds mixed in. I became a Christian in 1981 & purchased this album along with DA's debut album as some of the first "Christian rock" I was exposed to. Even back then I was amazed at the quality of the recordings & the bands ability to address spiritual issues via a popular music venue. But what truly sold me on DANIEL AMOS was their lyrical content being straight forward & truthful, exposing what they as a band of Christian performers were experiencing in their spiritual lives. The bulk of the theme of SHOTGUN ANGEL as an album is centered around the coming of the end times(the tribulation & appearance of the anti-christ).That's a very difficult subject even for some preachers to deal with but DA covered the subject realistically & simply,exposing others to the biblical truth of the matter. Some of DA's later releases were very different in content and music style and therefore lost my interest but even 30+ years later the sound & content of SHOTGUN ANGEL is still real & the message is valid. Some of the filler content that documents the history of the band, though very raw & unmastered does show the developement & growth of the band & their writing & performing abilities. As a Christian with a degree in ministry & having served in a number of music and discipleship ministries, I still find the music and lyrical content both pleasing and spiritually challenging. I highly recommend this re-issue & the DANIEL AMOS debut re-issue to anyone.

I first listened to the Daniel Amos masterpiece, "Shotgun Angel," in 1977 shortly after its release on vinyl.  It would be a good 35 years before listening to it again. This record has lost none of its musical relevance nor does it sound the least bit dated as so many of Daniel Amos' future recordings do.

Not that being dated is necessarily a bad thing.  It's not.  DA responded to the times with music and a message that is as relevant today as it was in the early 1980's.  This took real courage and commitment on their part, especially given the mindset of the Contemporary Christian Music (CCM) establishment during those early years.  Original Christian artists were often judged and even accused of losing their faith for straying beyond the accepted bounds of Christian Music normalcy.  Thank God DA did not lose sight of their vision and buckle under the pressure.  Music (and Christian Music in particular) is far richer for it.

There have been more than a few comparisons drawn between "Shotgun Angel" and other pinnacle rock records of the 60's and 70's, mostly due to the operatic theme of side two.  I disagree that it is inspired directly by any of these works.  It sounds nothing like them.  Perhaps it is the `thematic' approach of side two and its similarity to the highly popular `concept album' that peppered the musical landscape of that era that feeds the comparisons.  Say what you will about "Shotgun Angel" and its similarities, I believe it is a work that stands very well on its own. These comparisons don't serve to make it any better than it already is.

And if there is such a thing as a `Desert Island Record,' this one would definitely top my list, right alongside "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band," "Tommy," and "So Long Ago The Garden."  Lofty praise indeed, but well deserved.  Terry Taylor and his band-mates put together an astonishingly refreshing and original work that has stood the test of time.  This is a great record.  Being a believer is by no means a prerequisite for enjoying it, but being familiar with the themes certainly helps.

Side one is a careful blending of the country-rock music sensibilities of their first record, "Daniel Amos," and the more rock influenced direction they were heading toward on side two.  They skillfully started with `what we knew' of DA and led us in a musical direction we didn't see coming.

It opens with "Days and Nights," an Eagle's sounding tune focused on the central theme of "Shotgun Angel;" waiting for Christ's return.  It is a theme fully realized on side two, but only touched upon here.  It is a clever blend of country and rock that is immediately acceptable and satisfying.

"Black Gold Fever" is a slapstick country tune that uses humor to make a serious point; that the pursuit of riches often comes at a terrible price- the expense of one's soul.  It is also their first real venture into the wonderful world of musical theater, a trick they will utilize fully on side two and in many future recordings. This approach will become a familiar hallmark of Terry Taylor/ Daniel Amos.

"Praise Song," is a common theme in Christian Rock, especially one's written for the contemporary church.  It is exactly what the title suggests- a song of praise and devotion.  Although not my favorite song on the album, I can and do appreciate the message and sentiment.

"Father's Arms" is a song for the unconverted or those still on the fence.  While cleverly exposing many of the fallacies of modern, humanistic thinking, it urges one to "Fall In You Father's Arms," the only place to find answers.

"Meal" is the anguished cry of a believer hungry for truth told with a manic, turn of the century musical style reminiscent of the soundtrack for "Oh Brother, Where Art Thou" with a healthy dose of Frank Zappa loony-ness thrown in for good measure.  I love this song.  It is so out there and incredibly creative.  A very heartfelt message coupled with zany music and lots of background chatter, sound effects, and craziness.

"Shotgun Angel" is a classic written by the late Bills Spouse Jr.  It is especially telling that Taylor and company decided to cover this song and name their sophomore record after it.  It is simply a great country song.  And this is coming from someone who doesn't especially care much for country music. It tells of a trucker's encounter with God and of his Guardian Angel's protection.

When I began this review, I realized that nothing I could write could ever adequately convey the strength and creativity of the second side of "Shotgun Angel."  It is simply too rich to be described in any way that does it justice.  It must be experienced for one to appreciate it fully.

When I first flipped my old LP over and started side two, I wasn't sure what to expect.  The first few bars of "Finale: Bereshith Overture" began and I thought, "Oh no... overdone orchestration that sounds like its heading down the road of another bad TV episode score." Boy, was I wrong.  What followed was a skillfully written orchestral overture that introduced the themes of the following songs in a way that can only be described as rapturous.  The depth of the composition and use of space immediately stuck me.  The only complaint I can voice is that it doesn't go on long enough.  They could have created another five minutes of this music and it would have worked beautifully. But alas, they were limited by the restrictions of the old vinyl LP.

"Lady Of The Sky" is a tender tribute to the Rapture of The Saints sung from the viewpoint of one left behind.  It is thrilling and chilling, uplifting and sad, all at the same time.

What follows in rapid succession are three songs, all of which deal with the aftermath of the departure of the church and the coming of the `Anti-Christ.'

"The Whistler" begins with the sound of a foul wind blowing and the mournful howling of a dog in the distance. Far in the background, a discordant choir sounds to the march of battle drums, calling to mind ancient voices of doom and despair.  It tells of the arrival of `The False Prophet,' a man who, through signs and wonders, deceives mankind and prepares the way for the `Anti-Christ.'  It is a dark and forbidding song, but an integral part of setting up the story that follows.

As it fades, we hear the cry of crows and howling wind, followed by footsteps as someone approaches a gathering of people, their voices slowly rise until they fill the sound-scape.  An excited murmur rises. "There he is," an unknown person says. "The Whistler."  The clamor of voices and the tinkling of cocktail glasses crescendo, culminating in the introduction to the next song, "He's Gonna Do A Number On You."  Those familiar with Bible prophecy know of the `Mark of the Beast.'  This song takes us on a somewhat light-heated look at the rise of `The Beast' and beginning of the end for mankind, culminating with the stamping of the masses with his mark.  There is a veiled reference to the prophecy in "The Revelation of St. John" to a wound on the head of the beast that is healed.  Scary stuff when you think about it.  The music draws deep from an array of musical influences, not the least of which is The Beatles; while some of the more manic lyrical content calls to mind Firesign Theater in their heyday.

"Better" is the testimony of those who use the Mark of the Beast and their sole means of conveyance at a grocery store.  It is another frenzied, humorous take on the scary theme of world domination by The Beast and the elimination of currency in favor of the control of a permanent mark or tattoo.  This song is very reminiscent of The Beatles, complete with the tone of the nasal piano and the overall instrumental arrangement.  If you're a fan of the `Fab Four,' this song will definitely scratch that itch.

"Sail Me Away" slowly fades in and, contrary to the chaotic sonic journey of the previous three songs, it is beautiful.  Lush with strings and the harp, it shares with us a conversation between lovers.  One has had a dream of the Second Coming and mourns the loss of his lover as he chooses `the pilgrims call,' and forsakes all others.  As the song fades, a synthesizer's falling tone marks the dropping of bombs, complete with barely audible sounds of explosions and gunfire.  It is dark and haunting.

"The record finishes with "Posse In The Sky,' another flawlessly executed country song that uses the classic Western Posse as a metaphor for the Return of Jesus Christ.  A showdown is exactly what some fear/ bad guys are rounded up and bound/ and suddenly there is a cry, oooh- look up. Look up.  Ingenious lyrics that proclaim the return of the King of Kings and Lord of Lords set to brilliantly executed music.  As the song fades, we're left with the sound of the wind and of a rider on horseback signifying that it is finished.

Amen!

Side one (back when there were two sides to every album) had good country flavored pop rock.  Side 2 has the amazing eschatalogical smorgasbord.  Very interesting, catchy and wonderful.

Alarma, doppelganger and Horrendous Disc may be better, but you have to put this one up there as well!
summary: Great country / rock / end times cd !

I don't hand out 5 star ratings easily and this won't QUITE get one but for reasons mostly related to technical issues with this reissue rather than the content of the songs themselves. This is the 2nd album from the group which sprang from Costa Mesa, CA based Calvary Chapel and saw them expand their more or less Eagles sound with more rock influence (think Beatles a la ABBEY ROAD).

The album was remarkably cohesive with it flowing together track to track, in some cases quite literally. (The final acappella harmony of "Days and Nights" butts into the train whistle that launches oil fever fantasy "Black Gold Fever" and the railroad crossing warning sound at the end of that track segues into "Praise Song", not to mention the last 7 tracks which function as an extended suite on the theme of Earth's final days much like the 2nd side of the Beatles vaunted ABBEY ROAD release.

The group utilizes clever wordplay. They take the idea of God's Word [the Bible] as LITERAL food for the soul amid the chewing and lip smacking sound effects in "Meal" and imagining an assembly line for the administering of the number of the Beast in "He's Gonna Do a Number on You" ("NEXT!" [stamping sound fx] "NEXT!" [stamping sound fx]..etc etc). They also craft dazzlingly beautiful visual imagery (he tells a woman who's been taken away to Heaven in the Biblical 'rapture' "Guess it was your destiny/To go where you are free") and the "posse in the sky" (the Horsemen of Judgement day finding and jailing the Devil and his sympathizers).

It all falls apart on this disc though due to mastering problems. The seamlessly crafted blending of songs and themes that made this album so special in its inital incarnation on Maranatha! Records (CD08727) falls apart here on this M8 Records reissue because of mastering errors that cause extra pauses between tracks. Imagine if there was a 2 second lag on tracks on The Beatles SGT. PEPPER between the title track and "With a Little Help from My Friends" and you'll understand why this is so problematic.

BOTTOM LINE:
This is without question one of the finest Christian rock CDs EVER released. That's why it should be well done in the reissue. It might be worth getting this to tide you over but eventually you're going to want to shell out the extra $$ to get the Maranatha! version.

(-1 star because of the remastering goofs..)
summary: A  sterling shining classic of Christian music

This has been my favorite Christmas album since I bought it at a Hallmark store in 1995. Who knew? It is a classic as much as the Bing Crosby and the Charlie Brown Christmas albums are. The real tragedy is that it is a rare and obscure title.  You can't really blame people because they don't know that Glen Close can not only hold her own with a world renown opera singer, but has a voice that is truly amazing, clear and bright over an orchestra and chorus. Why hasn't she produced other albums? The orchestra, chorus and recording are superb, every song is wonderful with "Ding Dong Merrily on High" an incredible finish. It's a crime they didn't make a DVD out of the performance.

If I ever meet Glen Close I won't gush over her outstanding acting, it will be for producing a classic, and my favorite, Christmas album which I listen to, over and over, every December. If you like full throated, joyous classic Christmas music, you must have this album.
summary: A Truly Classic Christmas Album, A MUST HAVE!

Ordered this on Saturday, Mar 10 for reshipment to my brother in law in Germany.  Apparently JD Blackfoot has somewhat of a cult status in Germany and no one can find any of his music anywhere.  Anyway, today, Monday, March 12, the CD arrived in my mailbox from Ohio.  It is signed by JDB himself.  My brother in law will be beyond thrilled.  Not my kind of music but playing it now and can recognize why JDB has a cult like following.  Great service from JD and Eileen Blackfoot.
I purchased this CD solely for The Song Of Crazy Horse.  I enjoy that long, long song but do not truly enjoy the rest of the album

What can I say but the song of Crazy Horse is a classic.  The recording is perfect and clear.  Love songs that tell stories for a change and this one is no exception.  Worth the money.  Thanks JD for remembering Crazy Horse.

Thank you JD.  I remember listening to the Song of Crazy Horse on vinly back in high school.  The Song of Crazy Horse is an ageless classic that my two teenage daughters now enjoy listening to. The song is a classic history lesson that needs to be told.  JD's voice and the instrumentals on this CD are just amazing.  Although I bought the CD for The title track the other songs are also great to listen too.  I highly recommend this CD to any music lover or history buff.

I was so thrilled to find this CD! I was told about it by a Dear Native American friend and she suggested that I might like it. I LOVE IT! The bonus was purchasing directly from the artist! I thank you JD Blackfoot, and honor you! A-Ho!

What a joy to listen to this album on CD! I'd forgotten just how moving the title track is for me - a tour de force composition and performance that gets me choked up every time. It's a hauntingly beautiful song with a powerful message. The rest of the original album tracks include some honky tonk-style rock, softer, slower songs, and even some humor. Just some good, solid music all around. The bonus live version of Crazy Horse is a great addition - wish I could have been at that performance! It's fitting that it was recorded in St Louis in the early 1980's - as my first exposure to JD Blackfoot music was through K-SHE 95 when I was in college in the area at that time.

The sound quality of this disc is great, and the autograph was right on the cover as promised.

I owned the LP from the mid 70's until I sold my collection 20 years later and I would not be exaggerating to say that I listened to side 1  hundreds of times. The music is beautifully arranged and the lyrics appropriately follow the plight of native Americans in the second half of the 19th century. " The Song of Crazy Horse" flows without becoming tedious and the vocals are clear. Sit quietly and enjoy. A masterpiece.
summary: A wonderful history lesson set to music

reviewText: I also am surprised that more reviews have not been created. Thanks to a friend in college (1981), I heard the work of JD Blackfoot. The Song of Crazy Horse is top flight musicianship and song writing. This album and the Ultimate Prophecy, not to mention other works, are a must have, for any music collection. KSHE, a radio station in St Louis, was responsible in part for the great popularity of JD's work in that area (and beyond). An amazing story in itself. One of my favorite albums. Highly recommended.

I can't believe that no one else has reviewed this album! The Song of Crazy Horse is a powerful and moving rock ballad! This and "The Ultimate Prophecy" are must haves for any well rounded music collection. Not everyone is familiar with The Song of Crazy Horse because it is a long song that many radio stations just could not find the time to play. I was lucky enough to grow up in St. Louis listening to KSHE radio where this was revered as the masterpiece that it is!
summary: One of the most moving songs of our times!!

reviewText:
I saw the two prior reviews, and, while I'm not much of a reviewer, I thought this album deserved more. So here it goes....
First, the title of this review is not an overstatement. Darn Floor - Big Bite is really one of the best albums ever recorded. No lie. No kidding.
OK, now what is it? It's mid-to-late 1980's new wave...well, sort of. Really, it's much more than that. It's a mix of experimental rock, 1960's pop-rock and 1980's new wave that, for the most part, sounds surprisingly fresh today. Much of it was many years (decades?) ahead of its time. And it was performed by some great musicians.
The album is almost completely guitar, drums and bass. There's some pan flute and a small amount of keyboards on "Earth Household" and accordion on "Pictures of the Gone World." The rest of the effects you hear are guitar.
Terry Taylor is right up there with Bob Dylan as one of the great songwriters of our time. And, really, he was at the pinnacle of his writing on this album. The songs on Darn Floor - Big Bite were inspired by several great and often obscure poets (and a "talking" gorrila). If you like deep and sometimes puzzling (in a good way) lyrics, look no further.
Greg Flesch is maybe the must underrated guitarists in the business. He's not what you'd call a "technical" player (although he does have the sensibility of a technical player), but more of a pioneer, inventing new ways to make noise. In a lot of ways, this album (musically) was his.
Tim Chandler is one of the top bass players in rock 'n' roll. He does things most won't and somehow makes it work.
Ed McTaggart is Charlie Watts. Well, not literally, of course, but, figuratively, yes.
And Terry Taylor. I've already talked about how amazing his songwriting skills are. But he's also a good singer. Yes, he's got a unique voice, but it's certainly not annoying. Far from it, in fact, it's a joy to listen to.
So there you have it. A deep and forward thinking rock album that stands the test of time. That's Darn Floor - Big Bite.
Oh, and I haven't even mentioned the great bonus disc....
summary: One of the best albums ever recorded

The masters of genre-jumping are at it again!
It would be very difficult for any band to follow up the four incredible DA albums in the Alarma Chronicles (Volume 1 - Alarma!  Volume 2 - Doppelganger, Volume 3 - Vox Humana, Volume 4 - Fearful Symmetry, released in 1981, 1983, 1984, and 1986), but Darn Floor, Big Bite (1987) slightly edges out these gems as my own personal DA favorite.
As the album notes tell, "Darn Floor, Big Bite" is the description of an earthquake, given by Koko the famous gorilla that uses sign language and word symbols.  I'm sure that this is a "concept album" but, as with many of DA's other projects, most of Terry Taylor's coded meanings go a few levels deeper than what I can interpret.
The album is kind of a mix of heavy guitars, punk / new wave, driving beat, and beautiful ethereal music (think somewhere along the lines of Enya's music) - it's amazing how DA combines these styles together and totally makes it all work!  Stylistically, there is cohesion throughout the album, and Taylor uses a different vocal style ("new wave voice?") than on most of his other songs.
Favorites are "The Shape of Air" ("I can sit and stare 'til it's almost clear," a reference to God?), "Safety Net" ("You fall, you get, caught in the safety net."  This one's not too hard to figure out, as it also starts with a reference to the "cradle of grace."), and Pictures of the Gone World.
I've often heard references to Terry Scott Taylor's "creative genius," and it is at full throttle on this album - I just wish he would explain more of the deeper meanings of his lyrics.  Sad to say, but this album has been in and out of print, and is currently out.
You can find more information about Daniel Amos, their many offshoots (bands and solo), and their music at their great website (easily found with a search or a little imagination).

This is an excellent studio album of the late/great Lynyrd Skynyrd Guitarist, Steve Gaines. Plus, you get 7 more studio back-up musicians. You get a song set of 9 great songs. This album was recorded 2 years before Steve Gaines joined the Lynyrd Skynyrd Band. It was not released until 1988. Steve, along with his sister Cassie, Ronnie Van Zant, and Road Manager Dean Kilpatrick were all killed in the October 20, 1977 plane crash.

Thank God, Steve left this album cd for us. He served as a excellent guitar player for Lynyrd Skynyrd, and even sung the lead vocals on one song, on Skynyrd's album "Street Survivors". Plus, he co-wrote some songs along with Ronnie Van Zant included in that album.

This album cd "One in The Sun" by Steve Gaines consists of the following songs:

1. Give it to Get It (written by Steve Gaines)
2. It's Alright (A Curtis Mayfield song)
3. Blackjack Davy (A Tal Mahal song)
4. On the Road (a John Moss song)
5. One in the Sun (written by Steve Gaines)
6. Talkin' About Love (written by Steve Gaines & John Moss)
7. Nothin' is New (written by Steve Gaines)
8. Take my Time (written by Steve Gaines)
9. Summertime's Here (written by Steve Gaines)

This is an excellent album cd showcasing Steve's very talented singing, guitar playing, and his songwriting. I consider it a real treat, and "must-have" for hard core Lynyrd Skynyrd fans, and I definitely am one. Thanks, and May God Bless!!!

Steve Gaines only solo release, "One in the Sun" is truly a work of nearly magical artistry. Ronnie Van Zant of Lynyrd Skynryd, who marveled at the vocal and instrumental skills of Mr. Gaines, Lynyrd Skynyrd's newest member, stated both publicly and privately that the band would "all be in his shadow one day". Steve's contributions to Lynyrd Skynyrd included his co-lead vocals with Ronnie on the co-written "You've Got That Right" and the rousing guitar boogie on "I Know A Little" which he wrote before he joining Lynyrd Skynyrd. so confident was Ronnie Van Zant of Steve's abilities that on the album "One More From The Road", "Street Survivors" and some concerts featured Steve delivering his self-penned bluesy "Ain't No Good Life"  one of the few songs in the Lynyrd Skynyrd catalog to feature a lead vocalist other than Ronnie Van Zant. Steve Gaines bluesy rock 'n roll, if he'd survived the plane crash, would have surely catapulted him to international stardom perhaps even rivaling other blues greats as incredible as Stevie Ray Vaughn. each track is a masterpiece. "One in the Sun" is a must have cd for fans of southern rock, blues or just classic rock 'n roll. I highly recommend this lone solo project, especially to fans of the original Lynyrd Skynyrd. my personal rating is a powerful Five *S*T*A*R*S!

I have listened to all of Steve Gaines's cds, 1) One in the Sun, 2) Okie, 3)I Know a Little. I have actually
thrown duplicate copies of the latter two cds into the trash simply because I thought the music was so
horrendous. People fell in love with Steve Gaines because he played with a great band for a year and a half.
Steve Gaines became a household name because he first played with Allen Collins, Gary Rossington, the band and
because he wrote some with Ronnie Van Zant. Steve was a good guitar player and he brought a lot to Skynyrd. Steve
expanded the range of Skynyrd for a short time. But then too so did Ed King whom Gaines replaced on guitar.
Skynyrd was always better with three guitars. The three guitar lineup fleshed Lynyrd Skynyrd into a rock
and roll contender. Sure, Allen Collins and Gary Rossington were great on guitar but something was still lacking.
The third guitarist fleshed out the band and completed and complemented it.

Of the three Steve Gaines cds that were released commercially, all I can say of them is that they clearly show
a musician who was making some very non professional or novice music. To my ears the music is mostly quite bad.
And of the choices for songs I can only ask where was this guy was coming from?

Steve Gaines became an instant LEGEND because he DIED after a short tenure with Lynyrd Skynyrd. In that short
period the man thrilled us by being at his peronal BEST. He wrote and sang "Ain't No Good Life." LEGEND, the
Skynyrd album of 1987 introduced us to Steve's song "One in the Sun", which is another decent Skynyrd song. Steve
also wrote "I Know A Little", and he was involved somehow in "You Got That Right" and "I Never Dreamed." This
was Steve Gaines at the HEIGHT of his professional career.

Now forget about the short Skynyrd tenure and you have a man playing what, The Holiday Inn or some bar. Ronnie
and Skynyrd RESCUED Steve Gaines from complete OBSCURITY. And let me say that Steve Gaines served Ronnie well
in a time when he had writer's block. Ronnie was somewhat exhausted musically when Steve joined the band. Ronnie
was the heart and soul of the band. Ronnie was the leader. Steve brought some personal MATURITY to the band. Steve
helped with some vocals and gave Ronnie the ONLY REST he ever got on vocals.

However, all three of Steve's albums/collections serve little more than to remind us of what Lynyrd Skynyrd did
for Steve Gaines. Steve may never have made it without Skynyrd. From what I hear of Steve's music I feel the man
probably would never have made it. Luckily though Skynyrd FOUND Steve via his sister Cassie Gaines. Cassie is the
one who told Skynyrd about her guitar playing brother.

Rest in Peace Steve and Cassie, and all the lost Skynyrd members.
summary: Skynyrd made Steve Gaines famous, and that is it.

reviewText: Steve Gaines is one of my favorite guitarists of all time, behind such greats as Jimmy Page, Jimi Hendrix, and Tony Iommi. This is a lot of praise for a man who was around for just 2 albums with Lynyrd Skynyrd (One More from the Road (live))and Street Survivors. We all know that he was tragically killed in the Skynyrd plane crash on October 20, 1977, along with his sister, Cassie, and Ronnie Van Zant. During his time in Skynyrd, he made an indelible impact, and was admired by band members and fans alike. Ronnie Van Zant was quoted as saying, "We will all be in his shadow someday." Of course, he was talking about his exceptional guitar playing. However, Ronnie had so much confidence in him, that he let him share in the vocals on some songs, and even let him sing his own song (Ain't No Good Life) on Street Survivors. His solo project, ONE IN THE SUN, is a different brand of music that highlights his versatility. It consists of mainly jazz fused with blues. I think that the album has an identity all its own, and standout tracks include On the Road, One in the Sun, Take My Time, and the cover of It's Alright. I've never been crazy about Steve's voice, but it still has a way of blending in nicely. I think that he oversings One in the Sun a bit, but this is minor. His great songwriting and guitar ability more than make up for the shaky vocals. Overall, it's a solid release, and is good traveling music. 8/10

Diana Ross shines brighter than the Christmas tree on this one. The CD is a combination of Miss Ross' vocals and lush orchestration by The London Symphony Quartet, Modern Jazz Quartet & the Kings Singers. Best track: "It's Christmas Time."

Originally a Hallmark premium, well worth the reissue.

Diana Ross sings six out of twelve songs on this cd, but for the price (99 cents plus S&H) I really cannot complain.
 If you are a fan of  Diana Ross and a collector than this is a 'must have' item. I was hoping for some better song selections but her previous Christmas CD  "A Very Special Season" has them and I basically bought this as bonus tracks. Her voice is very angelic and well suited for Christmas carols. Delivery was prompt and exactly as described, "Used, in good condition" is not something I usually would think to purchase but again for the price I took the chance. Glad I did, if you're a fan you know that you have to buy her music
on line because they certainly aren't selling it in the stores.

Whenever I can't find anything I'm looking for Amazon always comes to my rescue, whether it be them or another seller they will stand by the product or make a return as easy as possible.
summary: Making Spirits Bright Has Less Of Diana Ross Than I Would Have Liked

reviewText: "Making Spirits Bright"  by Diana Ross was a pleasant surprise.  It was much better than her other solo Christmas CD.  Diana's voice was in good form throughout the CD.
summary: Making Spirits Bright by Diana Ross

reviewText:
I can say that this Christmas CD, is so very memorable.
The first copy I ever obtained, came from HallMark, during a Christmas Special they ran at their stores.  I took it home and listened to the music, over and over.  There was one song, which has meant the most of all to me, "I heard the Bells, on Christmas Day".  Probably, because I had just lost my mother, and this song, said it all. For those who have lost a dear loved one, especially during or around the Holiday Season, I encounrage you to listen hear, the depth, and meaning this song represents.  As we all know, there are some voices which can move the spirit, like Ms Ross.
Enjoyed the CD, traditional Ross fare. For Collector's a must have. Price was excellent, but expected new as listed but received a used copy.
summary: Enjoyed Diana, but too many other performers

reviewText: This CD, originally a Hallmark store special offering, features Diana on  6 tracks: sleigh ride/jingle bells medley, the first noel, it's Christmas time, go tell it on the mountain, o little town of Bethlehem, and I heard the bells. The best part about this is that none of these songs is covered on her own "A Very Special Season" CD. So combine both CDs, and you have TWENTY Christmas songs recorded by Diana in 1994!
summary: more Diana Christmas tracks--a perfect complement to "A very Special Season" CD

reviewText: I got my first taste of Jason Morant at Aquire the Fire in Dallas. In his music you can truely feel his heart. He perofrmed some of the songs from the album and I purchased the CD rigth away. I Am Yours is a great song expressing Jason's devotion to God. His remake of Bless The Lord is another great track. This is a CD you can pop in and let it play all the way through.

This is one of the best Christian albums I've ever heard. Unbelievable. I don't say that lightly. There is a combination of musical quality and lyrics that is outstanding.

The tunes are unique. They are not at all trite, like something you've heard before. They are very pleasing to the ear. The production of the album is meticulous. The instrumentation is good. But especially the vocals are outstanding. Jason's vocals are passionate, reflective, powerful, and diverse. He uses his vocals as a fine instrument.

The lyrics are equally excellent. They reflect a heart that loves God for the deliverance that God has done in his soul. And the concepts Jason uses are very biblical. Let me give an example:

"Now I walk alongside my Father

Without fear of what may come tomorrow

Because I know even in death I'm alive

Because You are inside of me"

In the context of the song, he spoke of God's overwhelming beauty, and also of God's mercy in calling him pure (justification by faith). Jason also spoke of how God had opened his eyes to see the daylight (new birth). Now, in the quote above, he calls God his own Father (adoption). He is not afraid of what may come, just as, for example, Jesus commanded in Matthew 6:25-34. Why is he not afraid? Because "even in death I'm alive." This is accurate, because, for example, when Jesus was about to raise Lazarus, he said in John 11:25 "I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live." And why does the believer live? Because "You are inside of me." In other words, Christ lives in believers via the indwelling Holy Spirit. Remember that Paul said that "Christ in you" is "the hope of glory" (Colossians 1:27).

In short, the musical quality and the great lyrics make this album a great choice in providing another avenue for your heart rise up to God in worship.

I've been listening to this album in my car for a couple of months now, and I'm waiting till I would prefer to listen to something else--it hasn't happened yet. I bought this album on a whim, not ever having heard of Jason Morant. I just listened a little bit through Amazon. If you want to sample his music more before buying, I suggest you go to Jason's Web site. Just type his name in your favorite Web browser and you'll get to it. It will give you longer snapshots of all the songs, and it will give you an idea of his musical style is something you would enjoy.
summary: This is one of the best Christian albums I've ever heard

reviewText:
This is by far one of the best worship albums I've ever heard. (up there with Hungry, Facedown and United's look to You) Every song is incredible, from the great music to the passionate and powerful lyrics, the whole composition and production on every track is superb. Jason is very talented, I would love to see him live. The great thing about this album is I take it to work, crank it up and I'm not ashamed of listening to it or telling people about it. (pretty good witnessing tool) It is not some cookie cutter, cheesey over polished "worship album". Yuck!, Anywho, My favorite tracks are um basically every single one. But if I had to pick just 3 they would be:

#6 Bless the Lord

#8 Fashion

#12 I delight *including the secret song

I would actually rate it 8 out of 5 stars! Oh Yea! If that were possible!

So do your ears/heart/mind/stereo/body/soul/neighbors/family and spirit a huge favor and buy this album!!!
summary: Your ears/heart /mind and soul will thank you!
